title: Pull-back commutes with transcript execution
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob) with output type $\alpha$, and let $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ be functions; write $p'$ for the pulled-back protocol over $X' \times Y'$ obtained by pre-composing each of Alice's and Bob's message functions with $f_X$ and $f_Y$ respectively. Then for every $x' \in X'$ and $y' \in Y'$, running $p$ on the pair $(f_X(x'), f_Y(y'))$ to obtain its syntactic transcript and then re-routing that transcript through $f_X$ and $f_Y$ into a transcript of $p'$ yields exactly the syntactic transcript produced by running $p'$ directly on $(x', y')$.
hypotheses_covered: protocol p over X (Alice), Y (Bob), output α
replaced:
Let $p$ be a deterministic communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$
(Bob) with output type $\alpha$, and let $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ be
functions, so that $\mathrm{comap}(p, f_X, f_Y)$ is the pulled-back protocol over $X'
\times Y'$. Then for all inputs $x' \in X'$ and $y' \in Y'$,
\[
\mathrm{transcriptComap}\big(p,\, f_X,\, f_Y,\, \mathrm{transcript}(p, (f_X(x'),
f_Y(y')))\big)
= \mathrm{transcript}\big(\mathrm{comap}(p, f_X, f_Y),\, (x', y')\big);
\]
that is, executing $p$ on the pair $(f_X(x'), f_Y(y'))$ and then re-routing the
resulting transcript through $f_X$ and $f_Y$ produces the very same transcript as
executing the pulled-back protocol directly on $(x', y')$.
